mainTopic: רבי יהושע בן לוי's teachings on ברכת כהנים and stinginess, and who is included in ברכת כהנים
overview: The amud opens by ending an earlier argument: the הלכה follows אביי and not רב חסדא about calling out 'כהנים'. Next comes a סימן, a list of keywords for a series of teachings by רבי יהושע בן לוי. He teaches that ה׳ desires ברכת כהנים, that a כהן who blesses is blessed, and that a כהן who skips the blessing breaks three מצוות עשה. רב adds that a כהן who never goes up may be unfit, and the גמרא shows the two views fit together. A כהן must start moving toward the דוכן during the ברכה of עבודה, and even a slight movement counts. Then come teachings about generous and stingy people, ending with the claim that the עגלה ערופה is brought because of stingy people who send travelers off without food or an escort. Finally, the גמרא discusses a בית הכנסת made up entirely of כהנים, who is included in the blessing, and whether barriers or standing at the sides matter. That last question is answered from a משנה in מסכת פרה, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The final ruling: the הלכה follows אביי, not רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The last words of רב חסדא's view are completed. Then the גמרא rules that the הלכה follows אביי and not רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The call for the כהנים] should come from them. The הלכה follows אביי, and the הלכה does not follow רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רב חסדא's view. Then it gives the final practical ruling on the earlier argument about calling the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling settles two separate points. Following אביי, the שליח ציבור calls out 'כהנים' only when there are two or more כהנים, not for a single כהן. Rejecting רב חסדא, who held the call must come from one of the כהנים themselves, the call may also be made by an ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: From them (here, from the כהנים themselves)

steps.whatToRemember: In practice we follow אביי. The call 'כהנים' is made only when there are at least two כהנים, and it does not have to come from a כהן.

phrases.english: should be from them.
phrases.notes: These are the last words of רב חסדא's view: the call 'כהנים' should come from one of the כהנים.

phrases.english: And the halacha is in accordance with Abaye,
and the halacha is not in accordance with Rav Chisda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier argument between אביי and רב חסדא, which began before this text.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows אביי against רב חסדא about calling the כהנים.

steps.title: A memory aid for the coming teachings of רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists keywords that help us remember the order of a series of teachings by רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: desires the blessing, platform, during the service, cup, recognizes, benefits, with a calf.)
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא gives a list of keywords, one for each teaching by רבי יהושע בן לוי that is about to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to a teaching that follows. 'Desires the blessing' points to step 3. 'Platform' (דוכן) points to the teaching about a כהן who does not go up. The rest point to teachings that come later on the daf. The list does not prove or argue anything; it only helps us remember the order.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, a list of keywords
The platform where the כהנים stand to bless

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to read these words as one sentence. They are separate keywords, each one a reminder of a different teaching.

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: desires the blessing,
phrases.notes: This is just a memory aid, not part of the argument. Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: platform, during the service, cup,
recognizes, benefits, with a calf.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the halachic ruling and begins a new series of teachings.

steps.title: הקדוש ברוך הוא desires ברכת כהנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי learns from a פסוק that הקדוש ברוך הוא wants the כהנים to bless the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: How do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא desires ברכת כהנים? Because it says, 'They shall put My name on בני ישראל, and I will bless them.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first teaching in the list. It brings a פסוק to show that ה׳ longs for the כהנים to bless the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the כהנים first put ה׳'s name on the people, and only then does ה׳ say 'I will bless them.' This shows that ה׳ waits for the כהנים' blessing and wants it.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing the כהנים give the people

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
desires the Priestly Blessing?
As it says: "And they shall put My name
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:27

phrases.english: upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מִנַּיִן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִתְאַוֶּה לְבִרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first teaching hinted at by the memory aid ('desires the blessing').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא desires ברכת כהנים, learned from 'וְשָׂמוּ אֶת שְׁמִי... וַאֲנִי אֲבָרְכֵם'.

steps.title: A כהן who blesses is himself blessed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that a כהן who blesses the people receives a blessing, and one who does not bless does not receive it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי also said: Any כהן who blesses is blessed, and one who does not bless is not blessed, as it says, 'I will bless those who bless you.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second teaching from רבי יהושע בן לוי. He gives a reward for a כהן who blesses the people and brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק was said to אברהם: whoever blesses his children will be blessed. רבי יהושע בן לוי applies it to the כהנים. When they bless ישראל, they earn a blessing for themselves. A כהן who holds back his blessing loses that reward.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will bless those who bless you

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Any priest who blesses is blessed,
and one who does not bless is not blessed,
as it says: "And I will bless those who bless you."
phrases.notes: בראשית 12:3

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁמְּבָרֵךְ מִתְבָּרֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching from the same רבי יהושע בן לוי series, also about ברכת כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who blesses ישראל is blessed. One who does not bless is not blessed.

steps.title: A כהן who does not go up to bless breaks three מצוות עשה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that a כהן who does not go up to the דוכן breaks three positive commandments, each taken from a phrase in the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי also said: Any כהן who does not go up to the דוכן breaks three positive commandments: 'So shall you bless,' 'Say to them,' and 'They shall put My name.'
steps.whatsHappening: This teaching matches the keyword 'platform' (דוכן) in the memory aid. It warns that a כהן who skips the blessing breaks three מצוות עשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three phrases in the תורה's section on ברכת כהנים counts as its own commandment. So skipping the blessing is not one failure but three. This makes clear how serious it is for a כהן to stay off the דוכן.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes up to the platform to bless the people
A positive commandment (something you must do)

steps.whatToRemember: ברכת כהנים is something ה׳ wants, it brings a blessing to the כהן, and a כהן who skips it breaks three מצוות עשה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for treating a כהן's duty to go up and bless as a serious, required מצוה, not just a nice extra.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Any priest who does not ascend the platform
violates three positive commandments:
"So shall you bless," "Say to them,"
phrases.notes: Both phrases are from במדבר 6:23.

phrases.english: and "They shall put My name."
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:27

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹלֶה לַדּוּכָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reward for blessing to the sin of not blessing; matches the keyword 'דוכן' in the memory aid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who does not go up to the דוכן breaks three מצוות עשה: כה תברכו, אמור להם, ושמו את שמי.

steps.title: רב: A כהן Who Does Not Go Up May Be Unfit
steps.stepSummary: רב says that a כהן who does not go up for ברכת כהנים raises a suspicion that he is a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: We worry that perhaps he is the son of a divorced woman or the son of a חלוצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a different way to look at a כהן who does not go up for ברכת כהנים. Instead of saying he is breaking מצוות, רב says we should suspect he is not a real כהן at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רבי יהושע בן לוי treated the non-blessing כהן as a sinner who breaks three מצוות עשה. רב reads the same behavior as a hint that the man is unfit for כהונה, so he may be keeping away on purpose. This seems to clash with רבי יהושע בן לוי, and the next step deals with that.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of a כהן and a divorced woman; a חלל, unfit for כהונה
Son of a כהן and a woman who did חליצה; also unfit for כהונה

phrases.english: Rav says:
We are concerned that perhaps

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ בֶּן חֲלוּצָה הוּא.
phrases.english: he is the son of a divorced woman or the son of a חלוצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same case as רבי יהושע בן לוי in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who does not go up for ברכת כהנים is suspected of being a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה.

steps.title: רב and רבי יהושע בן לוי Speak About Different Cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that there is no argument: רבי יהושע בן לוי means a כהן who goes up sometimes, and רב means one who never goes up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not argue. This one is about a כהן who goes up from time to time. That one is about a כהן who does not go up even from time to time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב and רבי יהושע בן לוי do not really disagree. Each one is talking about a different kind of כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a כהן goes up sometimes, he is clearly a real כהן, so skipping means he is breaking the מצוות (רבי יהושע בן לוי). If he never goes up at all, that pattern makes us suspect he knows he is unfit (רב). The behavior is the same, but how often it happens changes what we conclude.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן who sometimes goes up and sometimes skips is a sinner. A כהן who never goes up is suspected of being unfit for כהונה.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree.
This one is where he goes up from time to time,
phrases.notes: "This one" means רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching about breaking three מצוות.

phrases.english: that one is where he does not go up even from time to time.
phrases.notes: "That one" means רב's suspicion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Removes the apparent clash between step 5 and step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each opinion speaks about a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like רב and רבי יהושע בן לוי argue about how to view a כהן who does not go up.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהושע בן לוי speaks of a כהן who goes up sometimes; רב speaks of one who never goes up.

steps.title: A כהן Must Go Up During the ברכה of עבודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that a כהן who did not go up during the ברכה of עבודה may not go up afterward, learning it from אהרן's blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Any כהן who does not go up during עבודה may not go up anymore. As it says: "And אהרן lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them, and he came down from doing the חטאת, the עולה and the שלמים." Just as there it was during the עבודה, so too here it is during the עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives another rule about timing: a כהן has to go up during the ברכה of עבודה (רצה), or he loses his chance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says אהרן blessed the people and only then "came down" from the קרבנות, so his blessing happened while he was still busy with the עבודה. In the same way, our ברכת כהנים is tied to the ברכה of עבודה in שמונה עשרה. If a כהן did not go up then, it is too late.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה of רצה in שמונה עשרה, which is about the Temple service
He may no longer go up
Just as there, so too here; a comparison between two cases

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Any כהן who does not go up during עבודה,
phrases.notes: "עבודה" here means the ברכה of רצה in שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: may no longer go up,
as it says:
"And אהרן lifted his hands toward the people
and blessed them, and he came down from doing
the חטאת, the עולה, and the שלמים."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 9:22

phrases.english: Just as there it was during the עבודה,
so too here it is during the עבודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹלֶה בָּעֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the next teaching in the series of רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who did not go up during the ברכה of עבודה may not go up afterward.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי אמי and רבי אסי Went Up Later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: is that true? רבי אמי and רבי אסי used to go up after רצה was finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי אמי and רבי אסי would go up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule using what two great כהנים actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי and רבי אסי were כהנים who reached the place of blessing only after רצה ended. If going up late is not allowed, how could they do this? Their practice seems to go against the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? A word that opens a challenge
But look, isn't it the case that

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי סָלְקִי!
phrases.english: But רבי אמי and רבי אסי would go up!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי סָלְקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule from step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule that a כהן who did not go up during עבודה may not go up afterward
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Real practice of great כהנים shows them going up after רצה, which seems to contradict the rule.

steps.title: Answer: They Started Walking in Time
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי started walking during רצה, even though they only arrived after it ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי would start moving their feet from the beginning, but they would not actually arrive there until later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining exactly what רבי אמי and רבי אסי did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They did start moving toward the place of blessing during רצה; they just did not get there until after it ended. So the rule is about when you start going, not when you arrive. Their practice fits the rule after all.

keyTerms.meaning: They uprooted their feet; they started walking
From the start, at the beginning

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rule is about arriving at the place of blessing during רצה. What matters is that the כהן starts walking during רצה.

phrases.english: רבי אמי and רבי אסי
would start moving their feet from the beginning,
but they would not actually arrive there.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי מֵעִיקָּרָא הֲווֹ עָקְרִי כַּרְעַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the facts: their practice was different from what the challenge assumed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אמי and רבי אסי seemed to start going up only after רצה, against the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: They started walking during רצה and only arrived later, which is allowed.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא's Teaching Supports the Answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא taught that the rule only applies when the כהן did not start walking; if he started walking, he may go up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is like רבי אושעיא taught: They only taught this rule when he did not start moving his feet. But if he started moving his feet, he goes up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבי אושעיא that backs up the answer about רבי אמי and רבי אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא limits רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule: it only blocks a כהן who did not start walking during רצה. A כהן who started walking in time may finish going up even after רצה ends. This confirms the answer in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this rule when...
He started walking (literally, uprooted his feet)

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן must start walking toward the place of blessing during רצה. If he started in time, he may go up even if he arrives after רצה ends.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for when a כהן may still join ברכת כהנים.

phrases.english: And this is like רבי אושעיא taught:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא עָקַר אֶת רַגְלָיו,
phrases.english: They only taught this when he did not start moving his feet,
but if he started moving his feet, he goes up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in step 10
steps.raayaObject: The answer that starting to walk during רצה is enough
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רבי אושעיא that the rule only applies when the כהן did not start walking

steps.title: A משנה about a כהן who is also the חזן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: a כהן leading the prayers may go up to bless if he is sure he can return to his place in the prayer without getting confused.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we also learned in a משנה: If he is confident that he can lift his hands and then return to his prayer, he is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה connected to רבי אושעיא's rule about a כהן who started walking. It is setting up the next move, which explains how this משנה fits that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks of a כהן who is the חזן and is standing in his place leading the prayers. It lets him go up and bless. That raises a question about whether he ever 'started walking' during רצה, which the next step brings up.

keyTerms.meaning: He is confident / sure of himself
Lifts his hands, meaning he says ברכת כהנים

phrases.english: And we also learned in a משנה:
If he is confident
that he can lift his hands
and then return to his prayer, he is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה connected to רבי אושעיא's rule from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אושעיא's rule that a כהן who started moving during רצה may still go up.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in ברכות about a כהן who is the חזן.

steps.title: But the חזן never moved from his place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier question on that משנה: the חזן did not start walking during רצה, so how may he go up?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: But he did not uproot himself (start walking)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reminds us of a question that was already asked on that משנה. If you must start walking during רצה to go up, how can the חזן go up when he stayed at his place?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי אושעיא says a כהן who did not start moving during רצה may not go up later. The חזן is busy leading the prayer, so it seems he never moved. That looks like it clashes with the משנה letting him go up.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (we raised a question on it before)
Uprooted, meaning moved from his spot to go up

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
But he did not uproot himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question on the משנה brought in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה allowing the חזן who is a כהן to go up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule requires starting to walk during רצה, and the חזן seems not to have moved at all.

steps.title: Moving a tiny bit counts
steps.stepSummary: The answer was that the חזן moved slightly. So too, רבי אושעיא's 'uprooted' includes even a slight movement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means he moved a little. Here too, it means he uprooted himself a little.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer: the חזן moved just a little during רצה. It then uses that answer to explain רבי אושעיא: 'starting to walk' includes even a small move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, you might think a כהן must really walk toward the דוכן during רצה. Now we learn that a slight movement is enough. This is why the משנה fits רבי אושעיא's rule and actually supports it.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן who did not move at all during רצה may not go up afterward. But if he moved even a little, he may go up.

phrases.english: Rather, it means that he moved a little,
here too, it means he uprooted himself a little.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means רבי אושעיא's rule, so starting to walk just a bit counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 and applies the answer to רבי אושעיא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (a slight movement counts as moving)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן would need to really walk during רצה, and the חזן did not.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a slight movement during רצה counts as starting to walk, so the חזן may go up.

steps.title: Only a generous person leads the blessing over the cup
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that the כוס של ברכה is given only to a טוב עין, learning it from a פסוק read in a new way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: We only give the cup of blessing to someone with a good eye to lead the blessing, as it says: 'One with a good eye will be blessed, for he gives of his bread to the poor.' Do not read 'will be blessed' but 'will bless.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי. Only a generous person should be given the cup to lead ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a generous person 'יְבֹרָךְ', will be blessed. רבי יהושע בן לוי reads it as 'יְבָרֵךְ', he will bless. So the generous person is the one who should lead the blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: The cup of wine held while leading ברכת המזון
Someone with a 'good eye,' a generous person
Do not read it this way (read it a different way)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
We do not give the cup of blessing
to bless with, except to one with a good eye,
as it says: 'One with a good eye will be blessed,
phrases.notes: משלי 22:9

phrases.english: for he gives of his bread to the poor.'
Do not read 'will be blessed,'
but rather 'will bless.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: אֵין נוֹתְנִין כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching of the same רבי יהושע בן לוי, about blessing and generosity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a generous person should be given the כוס של ברכה to lead ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Even birds recognize stingy people
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches from a פסוק that even birds recognize צרי העין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: From where do we know that even birds recognize stingy people? As it says: 'For in vain the net is spread before the eyes of every winged creature.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי: even birds can tell who is stingy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a net spread out is 'in vain' in the eyes of birds. רבי יהושע בן לוי reads this as birds sensing the stinginess of the person who set it, so they stay away.

keyTerms.meaning: People with a 'narrow eye,' stingy people
The net is spread out (with seeds on it)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
From where do we know that even birds
recognize stingy people?
As it says: 'For in vain the net is spread
phrases.notes: משלי 1:17

phrases.english: in the eyes of every winged creature.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ עוֹפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of רבי יהושע בן לוי's teachings, now about stingy people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even birds recognize stingy people, learned from משלי 1:17.

steps.title: Benefiting from a stingy person breaks a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that anyone who benefits from a צר עין breaks a לאו, from a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Anyone who benefits from stingy people breaks a prohibition, as it says: 'Do not eat the bread of one with an evil eye... for as he calculates in his soul, so is he; "Eat and drink," he will say to you...'
steps.whatsHappening: A third teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי: it is forbidden to benefit from a stingy person's food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק commands 'do not eat the bread of one with an evil eye.' He may tell you 'eat and drink,' but he does not really mean it. So taking from him breaks this לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: One with an 'evil eye,' a stingy person

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Anyone who benefits from stingy people
breaks a prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַל תִּלְחַם אֶת לֶחֶם רַע עָיִן וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: as it says: 'Do not eat the bread of one with an evil eye, etc.,
phrases.notes: משלי 23:6-7. 'וגו׳' means the פסוק goes on, but the גמרא skips that part here.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי כְּמוֹ שָׁעַר בְּנַפְשׁוֹ כֶּן הוּא
phrases.english: for as he calculates in his soul, so is he;
"Eat and drink," he will say to you, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל הַנֶּהֱנֶה מִצָּרֵי הָעַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of stingy people with a rule against benefiting from them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Benefiting from a stingy person breaks one לאו.

steps.title: Actually, two prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says benefiting from a stingy person breaks two לאוין: 'do not eat' and 'do not desire.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: He breaks two prohibitions: 'Do not eat' and 'Do not desire.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds to רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching. He says there are two prohibitions here, not one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק has two 'do not' phrases: 'אל תלחם', do not eat his bread, and 'ואל תתאו', do not desire his delicacies. רב נחמן בר יצחק counts each one as a separate לאו.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי: benefiting from a stingy person breaks one לאו. רב נחמן בר יצחק: it breaks two, 'אל תלחם' and 'ואל תתאו'.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
He breaks two prohibitions:
'Do not eat' and 'Do not desire.'
phrases.notes: 'Do not desire his delicacies' is in the part of the פסוק that the גמרא skipped with 'וגו׳'.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: עוֹבֵר בִּשְׁנֵי לָאוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to step 17 by counting two prohibitions in the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Benefiting from a stingy person breaks two לאוין: 'אל תלחם' and 'ואל תתאו'.

steps.title: The broken-neck heifer comes only because of stingy people
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that the עגלה ערופה is brought only because of צרי העין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי also said: The עגלה ערופה is brought only because of stingy people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רבי יהושע בן לוי about stingy people. He says the whole מצוה of עגלה ערופה exists because of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of the earlier steps about the צר עין. Here רבי יהושע בן לוי makes a surprising claim: a murder victim found between cities is linked to stinginess. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A calf whose neck is broken. It is brought when a murdered person is found and the killer is unknown.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The heifer whose neck is broken is not brought
except because of stingy people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the series by רבי יהושע בן לוי about the צר עין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצוה of עגלה ערופה is caused by stingy people.

steps.title: Proof from the elders' declaration
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'our hands did not spill this blood' cannot mean the elders are suspected of murder. It must mean they did not send the victim away without food or an escort.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And they shall answer and say: Our hands did not spill this blood.' Would anyone think the elders of the court are murderers? Rather, they mean: he did not come to us and we sent him away, and we did not see him and leave him. He did not come to us and we sent him off without food. We did not see him and leave him without an escort.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי proves his statement from the declaration the elders make. He shows it is really about hospitality, not about murder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one suspects the זקני בית דין of killing someone, so the declaration must mean something else. It means: we did not cause his death by refusing him food or an escort. That kind of neglect is exactly what a צר עין does, so the עגלה ערופה is brought because of him.
steps.whatToRemember: The elders' declaration is really about hospitality. Sending someone off without food or an escort can count as having a part in his death.

phrases.english: As it is said:
"And they shall answer and say,
phrases.notes: דברים 21:7

phrases.aramaic: יָדֵינוּ לֹא שָׁפְכוּ אֶת הַדָּם הַזֶּה״.
phrases.english: our hands did not spill this blood."
But would it enter our minds

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁזִּקְנֵי בֵּית דִּין שׁוֹפְכֵי דָמִים הֵם?
phrases.english: that the elders of the court are murderers?
Rather: he did not come to us and we sent him away,
and we did not see him and leave him.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּא לְיָדֵינוּ וּפְטַרְנוּהוּ בְּלֹא מְזוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: He did not come to us and we sent him off without food,
we did not see him and leave him without an escort.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק that proves the statement in step 19
steps.raayaObject: That the עגלה ערופה is brought because of stingy people
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 21:7: the elders cannot be suspected of murder, so the declaration must be about food and escort

steps.title: A synagogue made up entirely of כהנים
steps.stepSummary: אדא in the name of רבי שמלאי rules that if everyone in the בית הכנסת is a כהן, they all go up to bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: אדא said in the name of רבי שמלאי: In a בית הכנסת where everyone is a כהן, all of them go up to the דוכן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about ברכת כהנים. It gives the ruling that when everyone present is a כהן, they all go up to bless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally some כהנים bless and the rest of the people receive the blessing. Here, if everyone goes up, nobody is left to receive the blessing, yet the rule is still that all of them go up. This sets up the obvious question that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The platform where the כהנים stand to bless the people

phrases.english: Adda said in the name of Rabbi Simlai:
A synagogue made up entirely of priests,
all of them go up to the platform.
phrases.notes: Going up to the platform means going up to say ברכת כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about ברכת כהנים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If everyone in the congregation is a כהן, all of them go up to bless.

steps.title: Who is being blessed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if everyone is a כהן, whom are they blessing?
steps.simpleTranslation: For whom are they blessing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the ruling in step 21. It prepares the way for רבי זירא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blessing needs someone to receive it. If every person in the room is up on the דוכן, it seems nobody is left to be blessed.

phrases.english: For whom do they bless?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the ruling in step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who receives the blessing when everyone present is a כהן

steps.title: They bless their brothers in the fields
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that they bless their fellow Jews who are out in the fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: They bless their brothers who are in the fields.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question from step 22. The blessing goes to Jews who are not in the בית הכנסת because they are out in the fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the blessing does not need its receivers to be in the room. People who are away can still be included.

keyTerms.meaning: Their brothers, meaning their fellow Jews

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
For their brothers who are in the fields.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing is for Jews who are out in the fields.

steps.title: Challenge: people behind the כהנים are not blessed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא with a ברייתא saying that people standing behind the כהנים are not included in the blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But אבא son of רב מנימין בר חייא taught: People standing behind the כהנים are not included in the blessing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי זירא's answer using a teaching from אבא son of רב מנימין בר חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people standing right behind the כהנים are left out of the blessing, then people far away in the fields should surely be left out too. This seems to contradict רבי זירא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (a word that opens a challenge)
But didn't he teach? (introduces a ברייתא as a challenge)

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתָנֵי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מִנְיָמִין בַּר חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: But didn't Abba, son of Rav Minyamin bar Chiyya, teach:
People who are behind the priests
are not included in the blessing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's answer in step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that people in the fields are blessed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If people right behind the כהנים are not blessed, people far away in the fields should not be blessed either.

steps.title: Forced to be away versus choosing to be away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that people forced to be away, like workers in the fields, are included. People who could face the כהנים but do not are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This case is about people who are forced to be away. That case is about people who are not forced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by showing that the two teachings speak about different kinds of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people in the fields cannot come because they have to work, so they are still blessed. The people standing behind the כהנים could stand in front but choose not to, so they lose the blessing. What matters is whether the person had a real choice, not how far away he is.

keyTerms.meaning: They are forced, held back by circumstances

steps.whatToRemember: People who cannot come because of their work are still included in ברכת כהנים. People who could face the כהנים and choose not to are left out.
steps.confusionAlert: Distance is not what decides here. Someone far away in a field can be blessed, while someone right behind the כהנים may not be, depending on whether he had a choice.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one is where they are forced to be away,
phrases.notes: "This one" is רבי זירא's case: the people out in the fields who have to work.

phrases.english: that one is where they are not forced.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דַּאֲנִיסִי, הָא דְּלָא אֲנִיסִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (forced versus not forced)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone not standing in front of the כהנים is left out of the blessing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only people who choose not to stand in front are left out. People held back by their work are still blessed.

steps.title: A contradicting teaching: only some of the כהנים go up
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי taught that in an all-כהנים בית הכנסת, some go up and some answer אמן. This clashes with רבי שמלאי's ruling that all go up.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב שימי teach: in a בית הכנסת that is all כהנים, some go up to bless and some stay down and answer 'אמן'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that seems to contradict the ruling from step 21 that all the כהנים go up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said everyone goes up. רב שימי's ברייתא says to split the group, so some bless and some answer אמן. Both talk about the exact same case, so they cannot both be right as stated.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he teach? (opens a challenge from a ברייתא)
go up (to the דוכן to bless)

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Shimi teach
of Birta deShichorei:
A synagogue that is entirely priests:
some of them go up,
and some of them answer 'amen'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back and challenges the original ruling of step 21, after the side discussion about people in the fields.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of אדא in the name of רבי שמלאי that all the כהנים go up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about the identical case rules that only some go up, so the others can answer אמן.

steps.title: It depends on whether ten are left
steps.stepSummary: If ten people would remain below to answer אמן, only some go up. If ten would not remain, they all go up.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is where ten remain; that one is where ten do not remain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each ruling is talking about a different size of group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שימי's case has enough כהנים that, after some go up, at least ten are still left below to receive the blessing and answer אמן. רבי שמלאי's case is a smaller group where ten would not be left, so everyone goes up and blesses the people in the fields.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (the cases are different)

steps.whatToRemember: All the כהנים go up only when splitting them would not leave ten below. If ten would remain, some bless and the rest answer אמן.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where a group of ten remains,
phrases.notes: This is רב שימי's case: after some go up, ten are still left below to answer.

phrases.english: that is where a group of ten does not remain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two rulings apply to different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two teachings seemed to disagree about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do not disagree. Whether ten would be left below decides which ruling applies.

steps.title: Back to the teaching about people behind the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא from step 24: people standing behind the כהנים are not included in the blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Going back to the teaching itself: אבא son of רב מנימין בר חייא taught that people behind the כהנים are not included in the blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a teaching it quoted earlier so it can look at it more closely. This sets up the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, this ברייתא was only used to challenge רבי זירא. Now the גמרא studies it for its own sake and asks what counts as being 'behind' or cut off from the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: the matter itself (going back to a teaching quoted earlier)

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: This is the teaching the גמרא used back in step 24. Now it looks at it closely.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מִנְיָמִין בַּר חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Abba, son of Rav Minyamin bar Chiya, taught:
People who are behind the priests
are not included in the blessing.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (as a setup for the questions that follow)
steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, תָּנָא אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מִנְיָמִין בַּר חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of an all-כהנים congregation and opens a new discussion of the ברייתא from step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People standing behind the כהנים are not included in ברכת כהנים.

steps.title: What blocks the blessing? Is a partition a problem?
steps.stepSummary: Tall people in front of short people do not block, and a תיבה does not block. But what about a מחיצה?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that tall people in front of short people do not block, and a תיבה does not block. What about a partition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists things that obviously do not cut people off from the blessing, then asks about one case that is not obvious: a partition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If standing behind the כהנים leaves you out, maybe anything between you and them also leaves you out. The גמרא says people and a תיבה clearly do not count as a barrier. A real wall or partition is a bigger question.

keyTerms.meaning: they interrupt / separate (act as a barrier)
the ark or chest in the בית הכנסת

phrases.english: It is obvious:
tall people in front of short people do not separate.
An ark does not separate.
What about a partition?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, אֲרִיכֵי בְּאַפֵּי גוּצֵי לָא מַפְסְקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the rule of step 28 goes: what counts as a barrier between the people and the כהנים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a partition between the people and the כהנים leave the people out of the blessing?

steps.title: Even an iron wall does not block
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that even an iron partition does not separate Israel from their Father in Heaven, so a מחיצה does not block the blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהושע בן לוי said that even an iron wall does not separate Israel from their Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about a partition with a statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even an iron wall cannot come between Israel and ה׳, then a partition does not cut people off from the blessing. So the rule about people 'behind the כהנים' is not about physical barriers. As step 25 explained, it is about people who could face the כהנים and choose not to.
steps.whatToRemember: A partition, even an iron one, does not block ברכת כהנים. Only people who choose to stand behind the כהנים, when nothing forces them to, are left out.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the people behind the כהנים. A wall does not block the blessing. What leaves people out is choosing not to face the כהנים, not having something in the way.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Even a partition of iron
does not separate
between Israel and their Father in Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A partition does not block. Even an iron wall does not separate Israel from ה׳, so the people are still included in the blessing.

steps.title: What about people standing at the sides?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether people standing to the sides of the כהנים are included in the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: what is the law for people standing at the sides?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question. We know those in front are blessed and those behind are not, but what about those at the sides?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Front and back are already settled, so the sides are the unclear middle case. The question is whether the sides count like the front or like the back.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them, an open question the חכמים wanted settled
Sides: people standing to the right or left of the כהנים

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
The sides, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means people standing to the side of the כהנים: are they included in the ברכה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling front, back and partitions, the גמרא asks about the in-between case of the sides.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are people standing to the sides of the כהנים included in ברכת כהנים?

steps.title: אבא מר בר רב אשי begins a proof from sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: אבא מר בר רב אשי starts to answer the question from a משנה about sprinkling purifying water.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא מר בר רב אשי said: Come and hear, as we learned in a משנה: If someone intended to sprinkle in front of him...
steps.whatsHappening: אבא מר בר רב אשי begins bringing a proof. This step only opens the quote, and the rest of the proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is a משנה about sprinkling the purifying water of the פרה אדומה, not about ברכת כהנים. The idea is to learn from how that משנה treats "in front of him" and use it for the sides in our case.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect the proof to be about ברכת כהנים directly. The גמרא is borrowing an idea from the laws of sprinkling, and the full point is only clear once the quote is finished.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּא מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Abba Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
Come and hear, as we learned in a mishna:
If he intended to sprinkle in front of him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question about the sides by quoting a משנה from a different area of law.
steps.raayaObject: Whether people at the sides of the כהנים are included in the ברכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת פרה about someone who intended to sprinkle in front of him (the quote continues next)
